paras.text: Essential Insurance Act and Market Audio Lecture
This is the chapter that controls whether a Michigan insurer can turn you down for home insurance, whether it can drop you after a claim, and what it must tell you when it does either.

Here is why it earns your attention. It sits behind almost every nonrenewal letter a homeowner ever brings you. When somebody hands you a letter saying we are not renewing your policy, the rules that letter has to satisfy are in this chapter. And most of those letters are checkable against a closed list.

Chapter twenty one, M C L five hundred point twenty one zero one and following, carries three names on the statute text itself: Act two eighteen, Essential Insurance, and No Fault Insurance. It was added in nineteen seventy nine, and it covers both automobile and home insurance. We cover only the home half.
Fifteen ideas. After most of them, a question and then silence. Answer out loud.
Idea one. A trap in the very first section.
Twenty one zero one is not the purpose section. People assume it is, because a chapter's first section usually announces what the chapter is for.
Open it and you find one sentence: the words and phrases defined in sections twenty one zero two to twenty one zero four have the meanings given in those sections. It is a pointer. That is all it is.
The definitions live across three sections, split alphabetically. Twenty one zero two covers A to D. Twenty one zero three covers E to I. Twenty one zero four covers P to U.
Learn that split, because the chapter's two biggest terms, eligible person and home insurance, both start with letters in the E to I range. Both sit in twenty one zero three.
Idea two. Who counts as an eligible person.

Under twenty one zero three, subsection two, an eligible person is the owner occupant or tenant of a house, condominium unit, cooperative unit, room, or apartment. Or the owner occupant of a building of no more than four residential units.
Notice the shape. It is personal and residential, and it tops out at four units.
Idea three. The carve outs, which are the menu a carrier orders from.
The statute then carves people out with a list worth knowing cold, because this is exactly what a carrier reaches for.
A conviction within the preceding five years for arson, conspiracy to commit arson, or one of the listed Michigan penal code burning and property destruction crimes knocks you out.
So does a successful insurer denial of a home claim based on arson or fraud in that same five year window. And insuring a dwelling used for an illegal or demonstrably hazardous purpose.

Refusing to buy enough insurance disqualifies, with three thresholds you should keep as a set. At least eighty percent of replacement cost under a replacement cost policy. One hundred percent of market value under a repair cost policy. And one hundred percent of actual cash value under a tenant or renter's policy.
Eighty, one hundred, one hundred. Only the replacement cost policy gets the eighty.
A nonpayment cancellation within the preceding two years knocks you out, unless the premium is paid in full before the policy issues or renews.

There are dollar floors on insured value. At least fifteen thousand dollars for a repair cost policy. At least thirty five thousand dollars, or another amount the director sets by rule, for a replacement policy.

Rounding out the list. Physical conditions presenting an extreme likelihood of a significant loss. Property taxes delinquent two or more years at renewal. And failing to keep a uniformly required club or organization membership.
Question. Name the three insurance to value thresholds in the eligible person carve outs, and which policy type gets which.

Eighty percent of replacement cost under a replacement cost policy. One hundred percent of market value under a repair cost policy. One hundred percent of actual cash value under a tenant or renter's policy.
Idea four. What home insurance means, and what termination means.

Home insurance here means fire insurance for a dwelling of the type just described, plus other nonbusiness coverage bundled into or endorsed onto that fire policy, plus whatever the director adds by rule. It excludes anything meant to insure commercial, industrial, professional, or business property, obligations, or liabilities.
A personal lines chapter through and through.
Now one more definition, and it does double duty for the rest of the chapter. Twenty one zero four, subsection five, defines termination.

Termination means a refusal to continue to insure for reasons other than nonpayment. It also includes shifting you to an affiliated company at a worse rate or with less coverage, unless you asked for the move. And offering worse renewal terms, unless you asked or the old terms are gone everywhere in the state.
Here is the key insight, and it is a structural one. This chapter has no two separately numbered systems for cancellation and nonrenewal. One word, termination, and one notice rule covering both.
That differs from the Standard Fire Policy chapter, which splits cancellation out into its own letter. Two chapters, two architectures. Do not import one into the other.
Idea five. The duty to insure, and the section number people get wrong.
Now the heart of the domain.
It is twenty one one seven. Not twenty one one eight, which is the automobile parallel. And not twenty one one nine, which only governs how underwriting rules get written and filed.

Subsection one says that, as a condition of keeping its certificate of authority, an insurer shall not refuse to insure, refuse to continue to insure, or limit coverage available to an eligible person for home insurance, except under underwriting rules built under this section and twenty one one nine.

Notice the framing carefully, because it is easy to overstate. This is not an absolute mandate to write every applicant. It is a condition on the company's license. And it protects only people who qualify as an eligible person.
So the two questions in order are: is this person an eligible person, and if so, is the carrier's reason on the closed list.
Idea six. The closed list of bases.
Subsection two is a closed list of the only bases an insurer's underwriting rules can rest on. Three of them.
First, the same criteria as the eligible person exclusions you just learned.

Second, the physical condition of the property. But only if the rule is objective, tied to the perils insured against, and keyed to a real code or manufacturer specification, regardless of the building's age. And a government compliance certificate creates a rebuttable presumption the dwelling passes.
That phrase regardless of the building's age is doing real work. Old alone is not a reason.

Third, for renewal only, the insured's three year claim history. And only claims arising from the insured's own negligence, or a failure, after written notice, to fix a condition tied to a paid claim.
Read that third one twice. Renewal only. Not a new application. And not just any claims, only ones traceable to the insured's own negligence or an unfixed condition they were warned about in writing.
Idea seven. The nonrenewal claim history numbers.
Here is the number that shows up on almost every restoration claim, so get the pair exactly right.

For nonrenewal, an insurer can use paid claim history over the preceding three years, liability claims excluded, if there have been three or more paid claims totaling three thousand dollars or more excluding weather related claims. Or three or more totaling four thousand dollars or more including weather related claims.
Three thousand excluding weather. Four thousand including weather. Three year window. At least three paid claims, either way.
Hear the logic of that pair. If you strip weather out, the dollar bar is lower, because non weather claims say more about the insured. Add weather back in and the bar rises.

One important caution. Subsection five indexes those floors to the consumer price index every sixth year from January first, two thousand six, by bulletin. So the statutory figures are the base, not necessarily today's certified numbers. Same superseded figure problem you met in the claims clocks chapter.

Work the example. A Detroit homeowner with three water damage claims in three years totaling five thousand two hundred dollars. Three claims, and five thousand two hundred clears the four thousand dollar threshold. So a nonrenewal on that ground is lawful, if the carrier follows the notice rule.
Question. Two paid claims totaling nine thousand dollars in three years. Can the carrier nonrenew on claim history?
No. The rule requires three or more paid claims, not just a dollar total. Two claims does not reach it no matter how large they are.
Idea eight. The other nonrenewal grounds, and two traps inside them.

An insurer can nonrenew for a dwelling unoccupied more than sixty days, if there is evidence of intent to vacate or keep it vacant. Note both halves. Forty five days with clear intent to return does not meet that bar.

It can nonrenew for an adjacent physical hazard, but only if the hazard changed since the policy issued. And here is the trap: residential property or traffic patterns near the dwelling can never be that hazard, however well documented. So a carrier pointing at a new apartment building or a busier road has picked something the statute rules out by name.

It can nonrenew when the insured failed to buy insurance in excess of eighty percent of replacement cost, but only under two conditions together. Buying more than eighty percent had to be a stated sale condition, and the insurer also has to sell a form requiring only eighty percent as its floor.
And it can decline or nonrenew someone who threatened, harassed, or physically assaulted an insurer employee or agent, if reported to law enforcement.
Idea nine. How underwriting rules have to be made.
Those rules follow a process, in twenty one one nine, and the process itself gives you leverage.
Every rule must be in writing, and an insurer cannot transact home insurance inconsistently with them.
They must be applied uniformly and without exception statewide, so every conforming applicant is insured and every non conforming one refused, once the information is available.

They get filed with D I F S for informational purposes, open to public inspection. And if D I F S finds a rule inconsistent with the chapter, it can, after a hearing, order the insurer to stop using it.

Sit with uniformly and without exception for a second. That means a carrier cannot apply a rule to one homeowner and waive it for another. And because the rules are publicly inspectable, that is a checkable claim.
Idea ten. Inspections.
Twenty one twenty one covers inspections.

An insurer inspecting dwellings to decide eligibility cannot pick which properties to inspect based on race, color, creed, marital status, sex, national origin, residence, age, disability, or lawful occupation. That applies whether it is a one time underwriting inspection or an ongoing sweep of existing business.
Inspectors get civil immunity, other than contract claims, for anything related solely to physical condition findings.
Idea eleven. Rating factors, and the trap that catches almost everybody.
Twenty one one one gives the closed set of factors a home rating classification can rest on.

Amount and type of coverage. Security and safety devices. Repairable structural defects tied to risk. Fire protection class. Construction, meaning size, materials, and number of units. The insured's own controllable loss experience. Use of smoking materials in the structure. Distance to a fire hydrant. And availability of law enforcement or crime prevention services.
Subsection nine lets an insurer use additional factors beyond that list, if the plan stays consistent with the act's purposes and reflects a reasonably anticipated change in losses or expenses.
Either way the plan gets filed with D I F S under twenty one zero eight, and an insurer cannot issue or renew a policy except in accordance with its filings in effect.
Now here is the trap, and it is the biggest one in this chapter.

Subsection four of twenty one one one bans insurers from rating on sex, marital status, home ownership, education, occupation, postal zone, or credit score. And people quote that list constantly for home insurance.
That list applies to automobile insurance only.
Chapter twenty one has no matching prohibited list for home insurance. In fact subsection eight expressly allows home risks to be grouped by territory, so geography by itself is not banned.

So what is banned? Redlining. In twenty one zero eight, subsection eight. Every filing must specify that the insurer will not refuse to insure, refuse to continue to insure, or limit coverage because of the location of the risk, and an insurer shall not engage in redlining.
Hold both halves, because they sound contradictory until you separate them. Territory may be used to rate. Location may not be used to refuse, discontinue, or limit coverage.
Question. A homeowner says her credit score cannot be used on her home policy because the Essential Insurance Act bans it. Is she right?

No. That prohibited list in twenty one one one, subsection four, is automobile insurance only. Chapter twenty one has no matching prohibited list for home insurance, and territory grouping is expressly allowed. What is banned is redlining, refusing or limiting coverage because of the location of the risk.
Idea twelve. The notice rule, which is one rule for both.
Section twenty one twenty three. And because termination covers both cancellation and nonrenewal, this one section does the whole job.

A termination is not effective unless the insurer delivers or mails written notice at least thirty days before the termination date, to the named insured's last known address, stating the effective date and each specific reason.
Both pieces. The date and the specific reason. A vague letter fails.
Shorter window for new policies. If the notice goes out within the first fifty five days after the policy was first issued, twenty days is enough.
Nonpayment terminations are carved out entirely. They run on whatever schedule the policy states, because nonpayment is not a termination as this chapter defines the word.

And here is a subtle check worth having, because it is the one people never think to make. A termination is not effective at all unless the reason conforms to the insurer's own underwriting rules. An insurer cannot invent an off the books reason, even a true one, and have it hold up.
Thirty days normally. Twenty inside the first fifty five days. Nonpayment on its own track.
Idea thirteen. Declinations, and immunity.
Before any of that, twenty one twenty two covers people who never had a policy at all.

When an insurer or agent declines to write someone, it must give each specific reason. A written application gets a written explanation. An oral one can get an oral explanation, but the insurer must offer a written one if the applicant asks within ninety days.
And refusing to even hand someone an application form counts as a declination, triggering the same duty. That closes an obvious dodge.
Now what protects an insurer when it gives those blunt reasons? Twenty one twenty four.

Insurers, agents, and D I F S staff get civil immunity for statements about an insured or applicant in a cancellation, nonrenewal, or declination communication, unless made with gross negligence or in bad faith with malice in fact.
That is why a blunt, factual nonrenewal letter does not expose the carrier to a defamation suit. The statute deliberately protects candor in those letters.
Idea fourteen. Where a homeowner goes to fight it.
Section twenty one thirteen, and get this one right, because it is easy to confuse with its neighbor.

It says a person who has reason to believe an insurer improperly denied them home insurance, or charged an incorrect premium, is entitled to a private informal managerial level conference with the insurer, and to review before the commissioner if that conference does not resolve the dispute.

If the insurer does not provide a conference and a proposed resolution within thirty days of the request, or the person disagrees with the proposal, the person gets a determination by the commissioner. And if either side disagrees, on request the commissioner must hear it as a contested case.
Its neighbor, twenty one fourteen, is limited to rate filings. Never merge the two.
One honest caution. Twenty one thirteen is written around an improper denial or an incorrect premium, and the text does not say whether a nonrenewal counts as a denial. Do not overclaim it.

Alongside the statute, the everyday route is D I F S's consumer complaint process. Try the insurer first, then file online or by paper form, or call D I F S at eight seven seven, nine nine nine, six four four two.
Idea fifteen. Forms, the pool, and the three licenses.
Three shorter pieces to close.

First, policy forms. Chapter twenty two, section twenty two thirty six. An insurer cannot deliver a basic policy form in Michigan unless it is filed with D I F S and approved, or thirty days pass with no director action, at which point it is deemed approved.

Personal lines forms must hit a readability score of at least forty five under a formula written into the statute, plus topical captions, an identified exclusions list, and a table of contents for longer forms. Use an unapproved or withdrawn form and the penalty is twenty five dollars per offense, capped at five hundred dollars per form series.

Second, Chapter twenty nine, the Michigan Basic Property Insurance Association, which the statute calls the pool. This is Michigan's FAIR plan. You will hear it called the market of last resort, and that phrase describes how it works but is not statutory language, so do not quote it as if it were.

Membership is not optional. Every insurer authorized to write the covered property and home lines, other than those writing exclusively under Chapter sixty eight, must belong as a condition of keeping its authority to transact insurance in Michigan.

Its home insurance underwriting program must let every qualified applicant get home insurance for qualified property in a convenient manner, with insurance to value floors of at least eighty percent of replacement cost for a replacement cost policy, or at least one hundred percent of market value, up to one hundred twenty percent, for a repair cost policy.
For basic property insurance, its premium equals the licensed rating organization's rate for identical insurance, plus a uniform, commissioner approved surcharge.

And since nineteen eighty one, before every residential renewal, the pool must notify the insured of their rights to get home insurance both in the voluntary market under Chapter twenty one and through the pool under Chapter twenty nine.

One trap here worth carrying. The pool's fraud denial disqualifier is stricter than the voluntary market's. It applies where the pool successfully denied a claim based on fraud or conspiracy to commit fraud, and it requires the denied claim to exceed two thousand dollars and exceed fifteen percent of coverage in force for a repair cost policy, or ten percent for a replacement cost policy.
Arson sits in a separate paragraph with no dollar test. And the voluntary market's arson and fraud exclusion has no dollar or percentage floor at all.
So the contrast is: pool fraud denial has a two thousand dollar plus percentage test, voluntary market has none.
Third and last, the licensed players, because this is where you personally live.

Section twelve zero one, in a different chapter, defines agent as an insurance producer, and insurance producer as a person required to be licensed to sell, solicit, or negotiate insurance. It separates an agent of the insured, an unappointed producer treated as representing the insured, from an agent of the insurer, an appointed producer representing the carrier.
And the trap you have now met twice: it never defines the word adjuster.

The adjuster license requirement is a separate section, twelve twenty two, subsection one. A person shall not adjust loss or damage under a policy of insurance unless licensed as an adjuster, with exactly five exemptions.

Insurance counselor is a third license, section twelve thirty two. Nobody can audit policies, give advice or opinion on coverage, or use words like consultant implying that license, without holding it, subject to narrow carve outs including licensed attorneys.
Producer, adjuster, counselor. Three licenses, three lanes.
And a restoration contractor giving coverage opinions and negotiating claim reasons for a fee sits in none of them. That is the sentence to carry out of this chapter.
Time for the rapid fire recap. Fast, as a self check.

Chapter twenty one, M C L five hundred point twenty one zero one and following, added nineteen seventy nine. Twenty one zero one is a pointer, not a purpose section, and definitions split across twenty one zero two, twenty one zero three, and twenty one zero four. Eligible person and home insurance both sit in twenty one zero three. Insurance to value, eighty percent replacement cost, one hundred percent market value repair cost, one hundred percent actual cash value for a tenant. Dollar floors, fifteen thousand repair cost, thirty five thousand replacement. Arson and fraud, five year window. Nonpayment cancellation, two year window. Taxes delinquent two or more years. Termination is one word covering cancellation and nonrenewal. Twenty one one seven is the duty to insure, twenty one one eight is automobile, twenty one one nine is how the rules get written and filed. Claim history for nonrenewal, three or more paid claims, three thousand dollars excluding weather, four thousand including, over three years, indexed by bulletin every sixth year. Unoccupied more than sixty days with intent. Adjacent hazard only if changed, and never residential property or traffic patterns. Rating factors are a closed set, and the prohibited list on sex, marital status, home ownership, education, occupation, postal zone, and credit score is automobile only. Redlining is banned under twenty one zero eight, subsection eight. Notice, thirty days, or twenty inside the first fifty five days, with the effective date and each specific reason, and nonpayment carved out. Declination reasons under twenty one twenty two, written on request within ninety days. Immunity under twenty one twenty four unless gross negligence or bad faith with malice in fact. Managerial conference under twenty one thirteen, thirty days, then the commissioner. Forms under twenty two thirty six, readability at least forty five, deemed approved after thirty days, twenty five dollars per offense capped at five hundred per form series. The pool under Chapter twenty nine, mandatory membership, eighty percent replacement cost or one hundred to one hundred twenty percent market value, fraud denial needs over two thousand dollars and fifteen percent or ten percent. And three licenses, producer, adjuster, counselor.
If any of the questions I asked gave you trouble, that is exactly where to drill.
